not a part: A fragment of a count at a position (pattern 14, '2-7 on each side of rachis'), with 'rachis' wrongly singularised. This is the same decision as 'per side of rachi' and 'on each side'.
not a part: A quality adjective (almost sessile) cut off from its noun ('12-18 pairs of subsessile pinnules'). The counted part is the pinnule (FLOPO_0985028).

This could mean two different things. 'With a terminal leaf' reads like a pinnate leaf ending in a leaflet, which would be terminal leaflet (FLOPO_0996015). 'Conduplicada/involuta' reads like the uppermost leaf blade of a grass culm, which is an upper leaf (FLOPO_0996003) or a leaf lamina. The examples do not show which is meant, and the two need different targets.

This is a misspelling of areola, which can mean many things. At 12-27 µm across it is far too small for a cactus areole (PO_0025353) or a leaf lamina areole (PO_0025392). It is more likely a sculpture unit of a pollen, spore or seed-coat surface. The examples do not name the organ.

The examples only say it is absent or present and never name the organ that bears it. 'Abaxial' together with 'terminal' does not fit the plain apex mapping used for 'terminal spine' (FLOPO_0985023). 'Apical spine' was also rejected on 2026-11-23.
The organ is not named. It could be a tooth of a leaf lamina, calyx, lemma or bract, and each needs a different container. 'Lateral tooth' was rejected for the same reason on 2026-11-23.

'Standard' is the Fabaceae banner petal (PO_0025324), but it is also the inner tepal of Iridaceae. The appendages being described (slender, 0.5 mm long, adnate, counted) are separate outgrowths, not a region of the banner. Mapping them to the banner or to its base would give the banner a length of 0.5 mm. No appendage class fits, and 'corolla appendage' was also rejected earlier.

'Retinacle' is a variant of 'retinaculum', which was rejected on 2026-11-14 for the same reason. In Acanthaceae it is the hooked funicle (jaculator). In Apocynaceae and orchids it is part of the pollinarium. 'Straight, 5 mm long' suggests Acanthaceae, which would be funicle (PO_0020006), but only the family settles it.

not a part: This is a position phrase cut off from its noun ('2 bracteoles at the base', '3 or 4 at the base'). The counted part is the bracteole or flower named before it, and the whole is the organ whose base is meant.

This is a depression ('apical hollow 0.2 mm', '40-50 µm in diam.'), not a part, and the examples do not name the organ it is in. Seed, fruit apex and pollen are all possible. 'depression' was rejected for the same reason on 2026-11-14.

The examples describe nipple-like projections of two very different sizes, 1-1.5 mm and 190-250 µm. These are probably a fruit or capsule apex in one flora and a cell or seed-surface papilla in the other. The organ is not named, so no single target fits.
The organ that bears the appendages is not named, and the counts ('2' versus '2 - ± 50') point to different structures. 'Lateral tooth' and 'corolla appendage' were rejected for the same reason.
not a part: A fragment of a phenology statement (how many flowers are open at once). The bearer is the flower and the statement is about timing, not a plant part.
A generic outgrowth up to 1 cm, on an unstated organ. It could be an emergence (FLOPO_0986107), a trichome or an appendage, depending on the flora. It needs context.
not a part: A quality, not a part: 'digitate glands' are glands with a digitate shape, and '3-digitate blade' is a count of leaflets or lobes (pattern 03). The counted part is the noun next to it.

A layer beneath an outer cortex in thalloid or non-vascular groups (Characeae, some bryophytes, lichens). Its meaning differs between groups and PO has no class for it. It may lie outside the plant scope, so do not ground it without the flora's group.

not a part: A fragment of a moss leaf statement: alar or other differentiated cells extend N cells up the leaf margin. The bearer (alar or border cells) is outside the word, and the number measures how far the region extends.
not a part: A fragment that gives the scope of a count: seeds per megasporangiate strobilus (PO_0005032), i.e. pattern 14 with seed as the bearer.
not a part: A time rate (flowers opening per day), not a plant part.
not a part: A fragment of a ratio statement ('blade 1-1.5 times as long as the sheath'): pattern 10, with leaf sheath (PO_0020104) as the second term.
not a part: A fragment that states incision depth as a fraction of the distance to the midvein. It is a relative measure on the lamina, not a part.
not a part: A fragment of a ratio statement (inflorescence 10-40% of plant height): pattern 10 relative to the whole plant.
'With 2 distinct basal lamellae' could mean orchid labellum calli, moss leaf lamellae (FLOPO_0986126 phyllid lamella) or other ridges. With one example and no organ, it is ambiguous.

'Bristlelike' is a quality (cf. setaceous FLOPO_0991124), and 'spine' could be a cactus areole spine (spine leaf PO_0025173) or a spine on a Cenchrus bur. These are different structures and the examples do not name the organ.

not a part: A density unit ('6–9 cilia per mm'), not a plant structure. The counted part is the cilium, which is the trichome (PO_0000282; cilia is a synonym) on a margin. This follows 'per cm' and 'per node' in the earlier reviews.
not a part: A density unit ('1–3 hairs per mm of width'). The counted part is the trichome (PO_0000282). Same reasoning as 'per cm'.
not a part: An area-density unit ('21–60 hairs/mm²') that goes with the hairs (trichome, PO_0000282) of some surface. It is not a structure.

not a part: A fragment ('5 longer ones') that refers back to parts named earlier in the sentence. It is a comparative without its referent, like 'shorter' and 'longer', which the 2026-11-13 review rejected.
not a part: The unit of a count ('culms 5–9 per clump'). The counted part is the culm (stem, PO_0009047). This follows 'per plant' and 'per shoot'.
not a part: The unit of a count ('perianth appendages 2 per stamen'). This follows 'per flower', 'per bract' and 'per segment'.

not a part: A quality: the degree of division of a fern frond ('1(–2)-pinnate-pinnatifid'). In '18–20 pinnate-pinnatifid pairs' the counted part is the pinna (leaflet, PO_0020049). 'Pinnate' was rejected as not a plant structure on 2026-11-13.
not a part: A fragment ('5 shorter ones') referring back to parts named earlier. It is a comparative without its referent, as with 'shorter', which was rejected on 2026-11-13.

Ambiguous without the organ. It could be a floral spur (FLOPO_0986133; petal spur PO_0025511), a short shoot (PO_0004701, which has 'spur' as a synonym), or a spur on a fruit or seed ('finely tuberculate', 'swollen tips'). Ground it only when the flora gives the bearing organ.
not a part: A ratio phrase ('1–4 times longer than seed'): pattern 10 with seed (PO_0009010) as the reference part. Same as 'times calyx' and 'times tube'.
not a part: A ratio phrase ('lobes 2.5–3 times longer than throat'): pattern 10 with corolla throat (FLOPO_0986110) as the reference part. Same as 'times tube'.
not a part: The second term of a length ratio ('petiole 1/4–1/2 total leaf length'): pattern 10 with the leaf as the reference. Same as 'calyx length' and 'leaf length'.

'Calli' was rejected as a generic part on 2026-11-13. 'Bifid' is a quality, not part of the name. If the orchid lip calli keep coming back, the remedy is a 'labellum callus' class, not this phrase. Plant callus (PO_0005052) is tissue-culture callus and does not apply.
'Circular' is a quality (PATO), and 'scar' needs the organ that left it: leaf scar FLOPO_0986052, pedicel scar FLOPO_0986113 or stipule scar FLOPO_0986116. The examples do not say which.
Same as 'bifid calli': the generic 'calli' (rejected 2026-11-13) with a shape quality attached.
Generic crests ('apical cristae 4–12', 'with 2 cristae'). The bearing organ (seed, fruit, lip, anther) is not given, so it cannot be grounded.
not a part: A count phrase ('1 flower per axil'). The counted part is the flower (PO_0009046) and the unit is the axil. Same as 'per axil' and 'per leaf axil'.

not a part: A count phrase ('palea with 5–40 hooks per keel'). 'Hook' was rejected as generic on 2026-11-14, and the keel is the unit. These hooks are hooked prickle-hairs (trichome, PO_0000282) on the palea (PO_0009038) keels, which can be expressed with pattern 14.
Same as 'bifid calli': the generic 'calli' (rejected 2026-11-13) with a shape quality (lamellate) attached.

Two generic part names joined by 'or' ('lobes or segments 3-8'). As with 'segment' and 'lateral lobe' in the 2026-11-13 review, they need the organ they divide (leaf lamina lobe PO_0025517, calyx lobe FLOPO_0986005, corolla lobe FLOPO_0986006, ...). The count only becomes a pattern 03 annotation once the organ is known from the record's context.

not a part: A position fragment ('2-4 per pinna lobe'). The part being counted (e.g. sori) is not in the word. Like 'per node' and 'per axil' in the previous review, it is a place for pattern 14 (count at a position), not a bearer.
not a part: A position fragment joining two places with 'or'. The counted part is missing. It is not a structure.
not a part: A position fragment ('1 per ultimate lobe'). 'Ultimate lobe' is itself generic and needs its organ (cf. 'ultimate segment', rejected 2026-11-13). The counted part is missing.
not a part: A position fragment. The ultimate pinnule is the pinnule of the last order of division, so the place grounds to pinnule FLOPO_0985028, but the counted part (sori) is not in the word.

Ambiguous: 'spine cells' are cortical cells of Characeae (outside PO), spines on a spore perine ('envelope' was rejected 2026-11-14 for this reason), or prickle cells of a grass epidermis. Without the taxon and organ there is no single class.

A fragment of 'terminal branches subtended by 4 ...'. The counted structures that subtend the branches (bracts, leaves) are not named, so the word grounds to neither the branch nor the subtending part.
'Subulate' is a shape (PATO:0001954) and 'marginal' is a position. The remaining 'tooth' is generic: PO has no tooth class, and the organ whose margin bears it ('on ...') is cut off.

not a part: A quality, 'nearly whorled' ('Leaves 3-5-subverticillate'): leaves crowded in false whorls. The number is parts per node of the axis (patterns 16/17), not a count of a part named 'subverticillate'.

not a part: The number of orders of branching of an inflorescence or shoot ('2-3 tiers of branching'). It describes the branching system, not a part. The branch axes it counts are second/third order inflorescence axes (PO_0006321, PO_0006322), but this needs a degree-of-branching measure, not a bearer.
not a part: A ratio fragment ('ca. 3 × as long as anther'). The anther is the target of pattern 10 (fb:towards), not the bearer. The bearer is the subject of the sentence.
not a part: A ratio fragment ('ca. 1/2 as long as beak'). It is the target of the comparison, and 'beak' alone is generic (rejected 2026-11-13).
not a part: A ratio fragment ('1.5-2 × as long as petals'). Pattern 10 with the petal as target.

not a part: A ratio fragment ('anther tails ca. 0.5 × as long as antheropodia'). The antheropodium, probably the Asteraceae filament collar, has no PO class. It occurs only as a comparison target here, which does not justify a new class.
not a part: A position fragment ('Branches 1 at lower nodes'), like 'per node' in the previous review. The counted part is the subject.
'Sac' was rejected as generic (2026-11-13). A conic basal sac may be a short spur of a sepal, petal or labellum, or a saccate perianth base. The examples (partly Spanish) do not name the organ.

Mixed senses: '2 basal spurs on filaments' are filament appendages, which have no class and are not floral spurs. 'Basal spurs 5-10(-14) mm' may be perianth nectar spurs (floral spur FLOPO_0986133, petal spur PO_0025511). One rule would mix them.

not a part: A quality adjective (denticulate lobules, denticulate scales), not a structure. The counted bearers are lobules and scales of an organ the clause does not name. 'lobule' and 'scale' alone were rejected as generic on 2026-11-13.

not a part: A fragment: 'ones' stands for a part named earlier (stamens, flowers). 'Fertile' (PATO_0000955) is already a context word for stamen, flower and so on, and 'fertile' alone was rejected as not a structure.
A generic 'segment' with no organ ('divided into 2-11 further segments'). It is the next order of division of a leaf, lobe or frond. 'segment' was rejected as generic on 2026-11-13.
not a part: A colour quality taken from a phrase that counts other parts ('1-3 pairs of green spines', 'green longitudinal stripes'). It is not a structure.

not a part: An arrangement with a count ('cupules in clusters of 2 or 3'), not a structure. 'clustered' was rejected in the same way. Use the quality clustered or fascicled (FLOPO:0991098) with a count of the named part.

A union of two different parts ('leaflets or lobes 3-11'): leaflet (PO_0020049) of a compound leaf or lobe of a simple one. The lobe has no organ. Like 'teeth or lobe' and 'lobes or teeth', it is not one structure.

A generic tooth of an unnamed organ (margin of a leaf, calyx or bract) plus the quality 'long'. Where the clause names the leaf, leaf lamina tooth (PO_0025518) with increased length applies. Without that it needs context.
not a part: A ratio fragment ('1/2 height of nutlet'): pattern 10 (ratio to another part), with nut fruit (PO_0030102, synonym nutlet) as the other part.

not a part: A position fragment of a count ('6-14 [veins or pinnae] on each side of costa'). The counted part is named earlier in the sentence. Costa is leaf midvein (PO_0020139) or costa (PO_0030072).
not a part: A quality (finely pilose) of domatia ('with pilosulous domatia'). The bearer is domatium (FLOPO_0986021).

The part of a rachis that extends beyond the last lateral member. It occurs on leaf rachises (paripinnate legumes: leaf rachis PO_0020055) and on grass inflorescence rachises beyond the last spikelet (inflorescence axis PO_0020122). 'rachis' alone was rejected as generic. Both senses use the apex region of the right rachis, but which rachis it is needs context.
not a part: A ratio fragment ('bracts 1/4-1/3 as long as seed scales'): pattern 10, with megasporophyll (PO_0009027, ovuliferous/seed scale) as the other part.
not a part: Degree of branching ('lobes 1-3 times forked'): the quality branched/dichotomous with a count of orders, as 'times branched' was decided. It is not a structure.

not a part: A tuft of hairs is a hair distribution, not a part: the quality bearded (FLOPO:0991118) of the organ or region that bears it. This follows the rejection of 'tuft' and 'tufted'. Where a seed tuft is meant, coma (PO_0020061) applies.
not a part: A ratio fragment ('internodes 2-4 X as long as leaves'): pattern 10, with leaf (PO_0025034) as the other part.
not a part: A ratio fragment ('4-5 × as long as sepals'): pattern 10, with sepal (PO_0009031) as the other part, like 'times sepal' and 'x sepal length'.
A surface of an unnamed organ: 'tapering or conical' and '1-8 mm long' describe some organ we cannot identify here. It needs its organ, like 'margin' and 'apex'.
A generic part that needs its organ. 'horn' was already rejected as a generic part in the 2026-11-13 review.

The word has two senses here. 'stem and pedicle glandular hairy' is a misspelling of pedicel (PO_0030112-type flower stalk), but 'Pedicle of the antheridia biseriate' is antheridium stalk (PO_0030035). One rule cannot cover both, so the word needs its context: map 'pedicle of the antheridia' to antheridium stalk and fix the misspelling elsewhere.

word: times as long as palea of lateral spikelet
reason: not a part: A fragment of a ratio, 'palea of central spikelet 0.7-0.8 times as long as palea of lateral spikelet' (pattern 10). The bearer is the palea of the central spikelet and the second term is the palea of the lateral spikelet.
not a part: A fragment of a ratio, '1-3 times as long as the bract' or 'bractea 2-plo longior' (pattern 10). The bract is the second term and the bearer is the part being described.

It is unclear whether these are comb-like ridges on hyaline cell walls (as in Sphagnum) or leaf lamellae like phyllid lamella (FLOPO_0986126). Mapping to either could be wrong, so it waits for a specialist's definition.
not a part: A growth form or habitat: mosses growing in hummocks. It is not a plant part. If used at all, it belongs with whole-plant growth form or habitat.
The teeth could be leaf margin, calyx, peristome or perigynium teeth. 'major teeth 0-4' does not say which organ they belong to.

word: rows of quadrate to rectangular cell
reason: not a part: A parsing fragment with shape qualities (quadrate, rectangular) inside the bearer word. The intended reading is a count of rows of laminal cells (FLOPO_0986100) near the leaf base, which are quadrate to rectangular. Fix this in the parser.
'2-3 layers of superficial cells' leaves out the organ, probably the moss stem cortex but possibly a leaf or capsule. The word is a fragment around a count.

not a part: '3-5-digitées' and '3 digitada(s)' give how many times a leaf or blade is digitately (palmately) divided. That is a division quality of the leaf counted by pattern 03, not a part. Same reasoning as 'pinnation' and 'ternate' in the 2026-11-14 review; 'digitation' was rejected then too.

'Collet' covers a ring or collar of the filaments ('collet des filets'), the base of a fruit or seed, or the root–stem junction. Leaf collar (PO_0006012) is the grass leaf structure and does not fit. The examples do not show which organ is meant; 'ring' was rejected as a generic part on 2026-11-13.
not a part: A shape quality (globose) of the appendages ('à appendices globuleux'). The part is a generic appendage, which was rejected on 2026-11-13.

French for massula. The 2026-11-14 review rejected 'massula': it has two unrelated senses (the Azolla microspore massula with glochidia, which fits these examples, and the orchid pollen packet) and only two floras use it. Keep it as a possible PO request.
not a part: A state of the bearer: young (PATO_0000309) is already a context word (pattern 04). 'Graines jeunes 2' is a count of young seeds whose bearer is the following noun.
not a part: The French or Spanish preposition 'en' ('en 2 lobes', 'en cada lado'), a parsing fragment like 'de'.

In 'dépassant le limbe stérile' it is a fern fertile part (the sporophore of Ophioglossaceae, or fertile pinnae or segments of dimorphic fronds). 'Division' is generic (rejected 2026-11-13), and which structure is meant depends on the family. 'Fertile' itself is the state PATO_0000955 (pattern 04).
not a part: 'Atteignant les 3/4 de la longueur' gives how deep a lobe or incision reaches, as a ratio to the length of the leaf lamina (pattern 10). It is a ratio, not a structure.
not a part: French 'à 1–5 reprises' = 'times': it gives how many times something forks (a degree of branching), like 'fois', which the 2026-11-14 review rejected.

An order of division without its organ, like 'secondary division', 'tertiary segment' and 'primary segment', which were rejected before. It could be pinnules, segments of a pinna, or inflorescence branches.

not a part: French 'stries' = striae, a surface marking. Following the earlier 'striae' and 'stria' decisions, it is the quality striated (PATO_0001410) of the part that bears it, counted with pattern 03.
not a part: A quality. 'Renflements latéraux' and 'swollen-ribs' are swellings or ribs of an organ that is not named, and 'swelling' was rejected as generic on 2026-11-14.
The examples don't say which organ the pit is on (petiole, leaf base, seed?). The 2026-11-13 review rejected 'pit' as a generic part, and 'adaxial' doesn't settle which organ it belongs to.

This is the generic part 'lobe' plus the shape 'filiform'. Like 'lobe' and 'lateral lobe' in the previous review, it needs its organ. If the organ is given, e.g. stipule lobe (FLOPO_0986076), the part is that lobe with the quality filiform.
This is the generic part 'sheath' (rejected before) plus the quality 'foliaceous'. It may be a leaf sheath (PO_0020104), a bract sheath or a cataphyll, and the examples don't say which.
not a part: Fragment: a count position ('flower 1 per fertile internode'), like 'per node' in the previous review, not a part.
not a part: Quality fragment ('bearing scales'). The part is the organ that bears the scales; the scales are a covering (scaly, PATO).
not a part: Quality of the secondary veins ('weak pairs of secondary veins'), not a part.
not a part: Shape quality of leaflets misread as the counted part; the counted part is the leaflet pair.
not a part: Shape quality of leaflets ('pairs of oval leaflets'), not a part.

The generic part 'bristle' (rejected before) at the apex of an organ not named here (usually the stipule). Stipule bristles in Rubiaceae are not always trichomes, so mapping to trichome (PO_0000282) is doubtful.

Ambiguous. 'Primary branch system' in grasses is a first-order inflorescence branch with its spikelets (near second order inflorescence axis, PO_0006321), but 'branch system' also means a shoot system. The context has to say which.
not a part: Fragment: 'of 2 kinds' says the parts are dimorphic, which is a quality of the set of parts, not a part.

word: times as long as the upper calyx lobe
reason: not a part: Fragment of a ratio statement (pattern 10). The other part is the upper calyx lobe (calyx lobe FLOPO_0986005 with a position).
Ambiguous: a sporangium-bearing region of a fern frond (possibly a coenosorus, PO_0025360) or a fertile zone of another organ. The examples don't say which.
not a part: Fragment: a count position ('seeds 3-6 in each chamber'), not a part.
Ambiguous: it is used for different stalk- or foot-like bases in different groups (inflorescence, flower, gland). The examples don't name the organ.

not a part: Fragment: 'ones' points back to a part named earlier in the sentence, which the snippets do not show. With counts of 10–20 it is usually secondary veins (secondary leaf vein PO_0020140), but the extractor should resolve the antecedent and not ground the pronoun.
not a part: Adverb ('up to 5 [flowers open] simultaneously'). It describes timing, not a structure.
not a part: Adverb of arrangement ('flowers borne singly'), meaning solitary. It is a quality of the flowers, not a part.
not a part: Spacing quality of the pairs (of veins or leaflets) that follow it, not a part.
not a part: Arrangement phrase. 'Leaves 4 in a whorl' is whorled leaves (pattern 16) with a count per whorl (pattern 14). The bearer is the leaf or branch, not the whorl.
not a part: Degree adverb modifying 'ascending' (veins). It is a quality, not a part.
not a part: Fragment of a comparison ('one half as long as the involucre'). It is a ratio to another part, pattern 10, with the involucre as the reference part.
not a part: A number word: about 12. The parser should treat it as a count value.
not a part: A 'per' phrase: 'stem 1 per leaf rosette' is a count with the reference whole rosette (PO_0025615), part_of in pattern 14. It is not a bearer.

Without context it is unclear which appendage is meant: connective (FLOPO_0986073), faucal (FLOPO_0986115), anther theca (FLOPO_0986131) or another. Once the appendage is resolved, the apex is a plain apex region.

In Combretum it means the primary radial walls of the peltate scales (a count of the scale's cells), but in mosses 'primary walls' are walls of the exostome teeth. It is a homonym, and PO has no cell-wall class for the scale count. Do not ground it without the parent word.
It means different things in different groups: the apothecial margin of a lichen (Ocellularia, outside PO), a flap round the staminal ring (Eschweilera) and a fern indusium flap.
Most statements are about Padina, a brown alga outside PO. The only other statement is about the outer edge of the leaf face in Lithops. Too heterogeneous for a rule.
not a part: A fragment of a ratio ('0.5–1 times as long as the leaf blade'). This is pattern 10, where leaf lamina (PO_0020039) is the second term.
not a part: A fragment of a ratio ('petiole 25–33% length of blade'). This is pattern 10.
not a part: A fragment of a ratio ('tube 9–17% of perianth length'). This is pattern 10, where perianth is the second term.
not a part: A fragment of 'alar cells 10–15 along margins'. It is a count at a position (pattern 14) whose bearer is the moss alar cells.
not a part: A fragment of 'fewer than 10 leaves clustered at apex' (Carex): an arrangement and a count of leaves, not a part.
not a part: A typo for 'body' in Juncus seed descriptions ('seed body clear to yellow-brown'). If fixed, the bearer is the seed (PO_0009010).
not a part: In Calochortus it is a colour patch on the petal, and in Marina it is an arrangement of glands. Both are a shape (crescent-shaped, PATO_0001870) or colour pattern, not a structure.
not a part: A fragment of 'arranged in 12–23 evenly distributed ...'. It is an arrangement quality whose head noun was lost.

not a part: Part of a count ('1 pleat on each side of midrib'). The counted part is the pleat (fold), and the midrib (leaf midvein PO_0020139) only says where. 'each side' and 'per side' were rejected before as not plant structures.
not a part: A count phrase. The counted part is flower (PO_0009046) and 'per cycle' is the unit it is counted in. 'cycle', 'per whorl' and 'leaves per whorl' were rejected before for the same reason.

not a part: A relative length ('1/2-3/4 length of petal spur'), so pattern 10 (ratio to another part). The petal spur (floral spur FLOPO_0986133) is the part it is compared with, not the bearer. Same as 'fraction of leaf' and 'calyx length'.
not a part: A count phrase ('1–10 per branch'). 'head' already goes to capitulum inflorescence (PO_0030121, C262), and 'per branch' is the unit of the count, like 'per node' and 'per head'.

not a part: The second term of a ratio ('proximal inflorescence bract 1/2-... inflorescence length'), so pattern 10. The bearer is the bract and inflorescence (PO_0009049) is the part it is compared with. Same as 'leaf length' and 'seed length'.
Small teeth between the main teeth of an unnamed organ (a calyx, as in Lythraceae, or a leaf margin). 'tooth' needs its organ, and 'interstitial' was rejected as a fragment before.
'ridge' was rejected as a generic part that needs its organ (2026-11-13). 'lateral rib' and 'lateral keel' were rejected for the same reason, and 'Lateral' does not supply the organ.
not a part: 'blade with 4 orders of leaflets' gives how many times a compound leaf is divided. That is a quality of the leaf (compound leaf), not a structure, as with 'orders of branching'.

Two kinds of part joined as alternatives ('leaflets/lobes 11–23'): leaflet (PO_0020049) for compound leaves and leaf lobes for lobed ones. A single rule would ground one of them wrongly. Same as 'teeth or lobe'.
not a part: A count phrase. The counted part is the leaf and the caudex (stem PO_0009047, C252) is the unit, as with 'per caudex branch' and 'per node'.
not a part: The reference term of a relative length or position ('widest at 0.4–0.55 length of body'), so pattern 10. 'body' alone was rejected as a generic part.

Spines on the margin of an unnamed organ: spiny leaf-margin teeth (Agave, Eryngium, thistles) or phyllary appendages. These are not spine leaves. The organ is missing, as with 'lateral spine' and 'basal spine'.
'rib' was rejected as a generic part that needs its organ, and 'median lobe' and 'lateral rib' were rejected the same way. 'median ribs 3' does not say whose ribs they are.

A generic word for a member of any whorl ('perianth members 6', '7-9-merous'), like the French 'pièce', which was rejected. Perianth members are tepals (PO_0009033), but the word alone also counts floral members of any whorl. '-merous' is a whorl count of the organ named.

not a part: A count phrase ('2–8 nodes between branches'). The counted part is stem node (PO_0020141, rule C254 on 'node'), and 'between branch' gives the stretch of stem being counted, which the patterns do not hold. It is not a structure.

not a part: The unit of a count ('areoles 8-10 per diagonal across midstem segment' in Opuntia). The counted part is the areole, and the phrase is not a structure. Same as 'per areole' and 'per segment'.
not a part: Two count units joined by 'or' ('1 per node or 2-5 per cluster'). 'per node' and 'per cluster' were both rejected as not plant structures.

not a part: The second term of a relative width ('1/2 to nearly equaling petal claw width'), so pattern 10. 'claw' alone was rejected as a generic part. Here the organ is the petal (PO_0009032), but it is only the part compared with.
not a part: The second term of a relative width ('1/3–2/3 petal width'), so pattern 10 with petal (PO_0009032) as the part compared with. Same as 'leaf width' and 'calyx length'.
not a part: A quality: plicate (PATO_0104365, synonym pleated). '5-plicate' is a count of the folds of the organ described (pattern 03), as decided for 'plicae'. It is not a structure.

not a part: A wrong lemma of the suffix '-porate' ('Pollen mostly 4-porate'). The bearer is pollen (PO_0025281) and the value is its number of pores, like 'celled' and 'ribbed'. A flora_counted_parts.tsv entry (porate -> pore on pollen) is the fix. 'pore' alone was rejected as generic.

not a part: A quality, not a part: reflexed (PATO_0104353). In 'reflexed spine rarely present' the part is the spine and reflexed is its quality; in '2 reflexed' the counted part is named elsewhere in the sentence.

not a part: The number counts rows ('hooked bristles in 4–5 circumferential rows'), not bristles. This is the same as 'rows of papillae' and 'rows of teeth', which were rejected before. The bristle is trichome (PO_0000282, synonym bristle) and 'hooked' is falciform (PATO_0002215, synonym hooked). Counting rows as bristles would give a wrong count.

'with 6 sac-like angles on proximal…': the organ that has the angles is not named, and an angle is a region of a surface, not a part. 'Sac-like' is the quality saccate (FLOPO:0991140) of that organ. It cannot be grounded without the sentence it comes from.
not a part: Part of a comparison ('± equaling length of seed body'), so pattern 10 (ratio to another part). The other part is the seed (PO_0009010) without its wing or appendage. It is not a bearer.

'with seed pulp red' can mean three things: a fleshy aril (PO_0009090), a sarcotesta (earlier mapped to testa PO_0020057), or fruit pulp around the seeds (fruit storage parenchyma PO_0025037, the earlier 'pulp' rule). Which one depends on the family, and the item does not give it.

not a part: A range of attachment qualities, not a part: sessile (sensu botany) PATO_0001436 to stipitate (FLOPO:0991065, synonym stalked), pattern 07. In '6–10 sessile to short-stalked', the counted part is named elsewhere. 'sessile' alone was rejected before as not a plant structure.
not a part: Same as 'sessile to short-stalked'. 'Very short-stalked' is closest to subsessile (FLOPO:0991013). It is a quality range, and the counted part is named elsewhere.

'1–2 smaller spines': 'smaller' is a size comparison with other spines, not part of the part's name. It is also not clear what kind of spine is meant. PO has spine leaf (PO_0025173), spine stipule (PO_0025174), spine petiole (PO_0025613), thorn (PO_0025172) and prickle (PO_0025169).

not a part: Part of a ratio ('no more than 1/4 spathe length'), so pattern 10 (ratio to another part). The other part is inflorescence bract (PO_0009054, synonym spathe). It is decided like 'times calyx' and 'times blade length'.

not a part: A count phrase ('spikes 1–4 per ray'): the counted part is the spike, and 'per ray' is the unit of the count (pattern 14, count at a position). The ray is a primary branch of the inflorescence. It is decided like 'head per branch' and 'flowers per cycle'.
not a part: Ratio of two dimensions of the same bearer ('1–1.2 times longer than broad'), so pattern 11. It is decided like 'times wider' and 'times as long as broad'.

not a part: Part of a ratio ('rachis widths mostly 2–3 times lobe width'), so pattern 10 (ratio to another part). The bearer is the rachis and the lobe is the other part. It is decided like 'times lobe'.
not a part: Part of a ratio ('up to 8 height of plant'), so pattern 10. The other part is whole plant (PO_0000003). 'plant height' was already decided as not_a_part.
not a part: A substance: a secondary metabolite in lichen chemistry ('with accessory substance'). It is not a plant structure.

not a part: A position phrase in a count ('often 2 at tip of branch'): pattern 14 (count at a position), with branch (PO_0025073) apex as the landmark. The counted part is named elsewhere. 'tip' is already a region context word.

'auriculate extensions at apex of…': the organ is cut off, so the auricle cannot be placed. It could be a leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106), a petiole wing or a bract lobe. 'Auriculate' is the quality PATO_0001981, and 'auriculate' alone was rejected before.
'with 2 basal backward subulate lobules': the organ that bears the lobules (leaf, bract, stipule, phyllid) is not named. Bare 'lobule' was rejected as a generic part that needs its organ.
not a part: a colour; the parts in the examples are veins and extrafloral nectaries
'base with 1 or 2 cupular sheaths' could be a cataphyll, a leaf sheath or an ochrea; the bearer cannot be told without context
not a part: a fragment: a quality plus a count per node; the part counted is elided
not a part: a relative-length phrase (male part as a fraction of the spike), not a part name
not a part: a fragment of '3-furcate', a branching-number quality
not a part: a branching-order count, a quality of the caudex (stem PO_0009047)
not a part: a fragment: says where the counted parts sit; the counted part is elided
not a part: a fragment: says where the counted parts sit; both the counted part and 'one' are elided

This joins two generic parts without the organ they belong to. The previous review rejected bare 'segment'.
'Short' is a quality. Without context the spur could be a floral spur (FLOPO_0986133) or a spur shoot (short shoot, PO_0004701).

'Spinulose' is a quality, and a 'projection' can be any outgrowth. The example does not say which organ it belongs to.
not a part: Spots are a colour pattern, which is a quality of the organ that bears them, not a plant structure. The previous review rejected 'spot'.
not a part: This is a fragment: two alternative parts joined by 'or'. They should be split into tooth and lobe, which are already counted parts.
not a part: This is a fragment: two alternative parts joined by 'or'. 'Segment' is generic.

not a part: This is an arrangement quality, not a part.
'With 2 winged flanges' does not say which organ the flanges belong to: fruit, seed or stem. 'Winged' is a quality.
not a part: This is a ratio to another part ('ca. 2 × as long as filaments'), not a structure.

not a part: A piece of a ratio ('petiole 0.5-2.3 × length of blade'): it compares the petiole with the leaf lamina (PO_0020039). The blade is the reference part, not the thing being described, so the parser should handle it as a comparison, not as an entity.
not a part: A piece of a ratio ('pedicel 1-1.5 × as long as subtending petiole'). Petiole (PO_0020038) is only the reference part, and the thing being described is the pedicel.

not a part: A colour mark, not a structure. 'with a yellow dot at throat' means the corolla throat (FLOPO_0986110) is spotted and yellow. The bearer is the part with the mark, and the quality is spotted plus a colour.

A ring at the base of an organ that isn't named. It could be a disc, an annulus, a corona or a perigynium. The previous review rejected 'ring' as a generic part, and 'basal' doesn't tell you the organ.

not a part: 'with 5-6 corners' gives the number of angles of a polygonal outline or cross-section. That is a shape quality (angular, with a count) of the described part, so 'corner' is not a bearer. The previous review also rejected 'angle'.
'lateral pits 2' could be on a seed, a fruit, a nutlet or a leaf base. The previous review rejected 'pit' as a generic part, and 'lateral' doesn't help.

not a part: 'c. 100 polygonal depressions on each [side]' describes a pitted or areolate surface (PATO areolate PATO_0002295, foveate PATO_0002296). It is a surface sculpture quality of the seed or fruit, not a structure.

not a part: 'with 5 rows of scales' / 'in 2 rows' gives the arrangement and number of rows of the scales. The bearer is scale or bract (PO_0009055) and the rows are an arrangement quality, so this is a phrase fragment, not a part.
not a part: A piece of a ratio ('endostome cilia to 1/2 segment length'). It is the reference of a comparison, not a bearer.
not a part: A piece of a ratio ('callus hairs about a third the length of the floret'). The floret is the reference of the comparison.
The upper region of a whole that isn't named: the plant, stem, leaf or pubescence. It becomes an apical-region rule only when the whole is known.
not a part: Verruculae are minute warts, a surface ornamentation (verruculose/verrucose) of the described part, not a structure with its own class.

The distal segments of a part that isn't named. The examples mix a leaf or stipule ('laciniate') with cilia counts that look like moss endostome. The previous review rejected 'segment' as a generic part.

not a part: Comes from '1-2 septate', a septation count of the described part (a hair, spore or fruit), not a mention of a separate septum. If ever needed as a bearer, septum (PO_0000030) already lists 'septa'.
not a part: A colour patch at the base of a petal or tepal: blotchy (PATO_0000329) on the base of the organ. It is a colour pattern, not a structure.
not a part: A position phrase ('1-3 below pinna midrib on apical ...') for sori or veins. The counted thing is missing from the word, so this is a fragment.
not a part: 'in 2-3 close pairs' uses 'close' as an adjective of spacing. It is a quality fragment, not a part.

A comparative ('9 or fewer pairs of lateral veins'). It belongs to the count of lateral leaf vein (PO_0006011) and is not a part. Rejected as a comparison word, like 'smaller' and 'shorter' in the previous review.

not a part: A measure ('occupying about 1/2 the leaf base'): the extent of some part relative to the leaf base (PO_0020040), i.e. a relation/ratio to another part (pattern 10), not a structure. Same as 'fraction' in the 2026-11-13 review.

Generic 'appendage' of a fruit (the examples cover horns and other outgrowths). It is a mixed group and needs the specific outgrowth; 'appendage' and 'horn' were rejected as generic in the 2026-11-13 review. The existing fruit beak (FLOPO_0986139) covers one kind.

The margin of an unnamed organ. 'margin' alone was rejected as generic. With the organ known it would be the organ's margin region with position inner (FLOPO_0991378), but the word alone does not say which organ.
not a part: A verb fragment ('0-6 merging down peduncles'). The counted structure is missing from the phrase.
not a part: A position phrase of a count ('1-7 on tip of upright shoot'; pattern 14 count at a position). The counted part is missing. Like 'per node' and 'per axil' in the 2026-11-13 review.
not a part: The denominator of a count ('1-7 per upright shoot'), like 'per node' and 'per plant' in the 2026-11-13 review.

A truncated abbreviation. 'Obliquely ascending, simple' suggests a fern rhizome (PO_0004542), but mapping a two-letter fragment for the whole corpus is unsafe. The parser should fix the source text instead.
not a part: A dimension used as a reference ('central strand to 1/3 stem diameter'): a ratio of the central strand to the stem (PO_0009047) diameter (pattern 10).
not a part: A ratio of two dimensions of the same part (pattern 11). The bearer is missing.
not a part: A ratio to another part (pattern 10). The reference part is the frond rachis, and the word is a truncated ratio phrase ('rachi' for 'rachis').
not a part: A ratio to another part (pattern 10) with a truncated 'rachis'. Not a structure.
not a part: A ratio to another part (pattern 10). The sporophore (fertile segment, Ophioglossaceae) is only the reference.
'ridge' needs the organ it belongs to and was rejected as generic in the 2026-11-13 review. 'Toothed' is a quality of the ridge.
not a part: A quality (extending down the axis below the point of insertion), not a structure. In 'decurrent lobe' and 'filets prolongés vers le bas' the bearer is the lobe or filament.
'3 ouvertures' could be pores of a capsule or anther, or pollen apertures. The bearer is unknown, like 'pore' in the 2026-11-13 review.

Already a contextual bearer for awn (PO_0025349) in reviewed_local_bearers.tsv. Here French 'arête' also means a ridge or sharp edge ('3 arêtes saillantes'). The two senses need context, so no global rule.
not a part: A branching event ('se bifurquant jusqu'à 6 reprises'): the number of dichotomies is a branching quality of the bearer (PATO_0001784 bifurcated, branched), not a part.
The edge of a fissure, but the organ (bark, anther, capsule) is not given. Generic, like 'slit' and 'margin'.

not a part: A relative measure (1/4-1/3 of the blade width), not a structure; it is a ratio to another part (pattern 10) with leaf lamina (PO_0020039) as the second term. The previous review rejected 'fraction' as not a plant structure.
not a part: A relative length (about 1/4 of the spathe's length), not a structure; ratio to another part (pattern 10) with spathe = inflorescence bract (PO_0009054) as the second term.

French 'group': a generic collection whose kind depends on its members (stamens in 2 groups = stamen fascicles; groups of spikelets = spikelet clusters). Like 'fascicle' (rejected 2026-11-13), it needs the part it groups.
French 'strip, lacinia': a narrow segment of whatever organ is divided (leaf blade, corolla, petal, stipule). Like 'segment' (rejected 2026-11-13), it needs the organ it belongs to.
'Crest' is a generic outgrowth rejected 2026-11-13; 'longitudinal' gives its direction but not the organ (fruit, seed, labellum, column). It needs the organ it belongs to.
'Petit rebord marginal' is a narrow raised border of some organ (seed, fruit, leaf, scale); the examples do not say which. Without the organ it cannot be grounded.
'Appendage' was rejected 2026-11-13 as a generic part. '3 pairs of small appendages' on the ovary is family-specific and rare (2 statements); no new class is warranted.
A generic protuberance ('proéminences ligneuses', '1-3 prominencias') of an unnamed organ; like ridge or crest it needs the organ it belongs to.
not a part: A shape quality (of a crest at the base), not a structure; mis-read as a bearer.

word: composed of a sessile spikelet and a pedunculate spikelet
reason: not a part: A descriptive phrase (fragment) about the spikelet pair of Andropogoneae. Its parts are spikelet (PO_0009051) with sessile/pedicellate as bearer qualities (pattern 04). PO has only spikelet pair meristem, and 2 statements do not justify a new class.
'Fleshy' is a quality and 'crest' a generic outgrowth (rejected 2026-11-13); the organ bearing the crests is not named.
not a part: French adjective 'large' ('8 grandes nervures latérales', '2 grandes'): a size quality or an ellipsis fragment, not a structure.

not a part: A fragment: a garbled token ('labellum' run together with another word); the examples ('bordes apicales engrosados', 'largement cunéiforme') describe the labellum or its lobes, not a distinct structure.
'4 or 5 scales' at the ovary may be hypogynous perianth scales, disc scales or bracteoles depending on the family; ambiguous, and 'scale' alone was rejected 2026-11-13.

'Swelling' says nothing about which part swells ('2 renflements at the base' of what). Without the part, it is a swollen region of an unnamed bearer. The swelling itself is a quality (swollen or gibbous) of the part named in the sentence.
not a part: Fragment of a ratio ('2.5 times as long as the anther'). The anther is the second term of pattern 10 (ratio to another part); the bearer is the structure measured, not 'times anther'.
Which organ has the cavity (fruit, seed, style, stem tip) is not stated. Without the whole it cannot be grounded; if the whole is known, it is an apex region of that class.
not a part: A fragment that describes how deeply an organ is incised (a split or dissected quality of the organ), not a structure. Counting splits is a count of lobes or incisions of the named organ.
Generic outgrowth of an unnamed organ. It could be an emergence (FLOPO_0986107), a tubercle (PO_0025352) or a lobe; too ambiguous without context.

not a part: Fragment: 'sessile' is a quality and 'lateral' a position; the noun (colleters, spikes, branches) is elsewhere or elided. The example '2 sessile lateral colleters' grounds as colleter (FLOPO_0986023).
not a part: A quality (elongated), not a structure; the bearer is the following noun (arms, colleters).
not a part: A colour marking ('chevrons (white markings)') on a leaf or bract: a pigmentation-pattern quality of that organ, not a structure.
not a part: A unit of mass (pound), the unit of a weight value.
A generic region word whose meaning depends on its modifier: 'stigmatic areas' ground as stigma (PO_0009073), 'área seminal' as the seed-bearing region. 'Area' alone is ambiguous.

not a part: A fragment: 'ones' refers back to a noun said earlier ('± 10 chief ones on each side' is nearly always the main lateral nerves). The parser should resolve the earlier noun. If it is a nerve or vein, the count goes to secondary leaf vein (PO_0020140), as 'principal lateral nerve' does below.

not a part: An arrangement word, not a structure. '11–12 concentric rows' is the number of rows the named parts (scales, tubercles, stamens) stand in. It belongs with the counted parts or arrangement rules, not with the bearer.
A generic surface depression that needs the organ it is on. The previous review rejected 'pit' for this reason. On a known organ, the surface reading is the quality foveate (PATO:0002296).
not a part: An arrangement ('in dyads or triads' means in groups of 2 or 3), said of flowers, pollen or the like. It is a grouping or count of the noun before it, not a part.
not a part: A position phrase ('8–10 in crown' means 8–10 leaves or fronds in the crown) that counts the noun given earlier. It is not a part in itself.

A generic bristle that needs its organ. PO seta (PO_0030032) is the moss sporophyte stalk and does not fit, and the previous review rejected bare 'bristle'. These may be lateral bristles of a lemma, a glume or an awn, but the examples do not say which.

not a part: A ratio phrase. 'Leaves 5–10 per tuber' is a count of leaves (the bearer is the leaf, or the whole plant). The tuber is the unit of the count, not the bearer.

Unclear without context. These are scars in rings or whorls of 4–9, perhaps of shed organs on an axis, but which organ is shed is not given. Neither 'pit' nor a specific scar class (leaf scar FLOPO_0986052, stipule scar FLOPO_0986116) can be chosen with confidence.
not a part: A fragment: 'primary ones 2' refers back to a noun said earlier (branches, veins, bracts). The parser has to resolve that noun.

not a part: A quality adjective ('3-pronged barbs' means barbs with 3 points; 'apex with 2 blunt ... prongs'). The bearer is the barb or apex. The number gives a count of points or a divided quality, not a part.
A generic surface outgrowth that needs its organ, like 'ridge' and 'pit' in the previous review.
A generic ridge that needs its organ; the previous review rejected 'ridge' for this reason. The 'radiating' side ridges are on an organ not named in the examples.
not a part: An arrangement word, and a lemmatiser fragment of 'series'. 'Tubercles in 3–5 spiral series' counts the rows of another part. The arrangement is spirally arranged (FLOPO:0991114).
not a part: A quality or event: 'with 1–4 splits' is the number of slits or divisions in an organ (for example a spathe or corolla splitting after anthesis), not a structure.
A generic outgrowth with no organ given. This could be sterile appendages of a spadix, a sporophyll or a receptacle, and the examples do not settle which.
not a part: A branching quality with a count ('6–8 times dichotomously branched'). It says how many orders of dichotomous branching the organ named earlier has, not a part.
not a part: A relative length: the bracteole is 2–3 times as long as the perianth. The bearer is the bracteole and the perianth is the reference, so this is a quality relation, not a part.

not a part: A compound shape adjective ('6–10 pairs of triangular-lobulate [segments]'): triangular with small lobes. The counted part is the leaf segment that follows. It is a quality fragment, not a structure.
not a part: A spelling variant of triangular-lobulate: a shape adjective that qualifies the counted segments, not a part name.

'The crest on each side of 3 lobes': the crest's owner is unknown (keel crest of Polygala, seed crest, anther crest), and the Spanish fragment 'ovados' does not help. It is a generic part that needs its organ.
not a part: An OCR misreading of 'μm' ('about 8 fj, wide', '31-36.5 fj, long'). It is a unit, not a structure. It should be fixed in the text normalisation.

Plant cell plus the quality 'large', with no organ ('about 4 large cells', 'cortical layer of 10-12 large cells'). Like 'scale' and 'segment' in the previous review, it is a generic part that needs its organ.
not a part: A ratio fragment ('espacées de 1-2 fois leur longueur'). It belongs to pattern 10 (ratio to another part), with the internode or spikelet as bearer.

'Rhizome composed of up to about t[en] units' and units 'claviformes a subglobosas': these are sympodial segments or tuberous swellings that change from family to family. PO has rhizome (PO_0004542) and rhizome internode (PO_0025204), but neither fits safely.
A generic outgrowth without its organ ('raised on protuberances ± 1 mm high'). It could be emergence (FLOPO_0986107), tubercle or wart depending on context.
not a part: A frequency adverb ('pairs of often anisophyllous...'). It belongs to the frequency of an alternative (pattern 8), not to a part.
not a part: A ratio fragment ('terminal one up to twice as long as the laterals'). It belongs to pattern 10, with the terminal leaflet or lobe as bearer and the lateral ones as the second term.
not a part: A density phrase ('commissural veins 8-15 per cm', 'environ 7 par cm'). The bearer is the veins and the value is a count per length, so this is not a part name.
A generic 'lobe' with a developmental state ('only 1-3 lobes developing'), without the organ it belongs to.

A generic placeholder ('some plant parts', 'several plant parts'). It does not name a part. Grounding it to plant structure (PO_0009011) would only make empty annotations. You can tell which part is meant only from context.

Unclear without the group. It could be a cone-scale apex, a bud scale or an involucral scale. 'Terminal' could be a position (PATO_0002476 terminal) on any scale-like part, but PO's 'scale' synonyms point to trichome, bract and scale leaf. It occurs twice.

This is a cell component, the wall of pith cells (pith PO_0006109, plant cell PO_0009002). PO has no cell-wall class (that is GO), and no pattern composes a GO component with a PO tissue. It is rare (2 statements), and the 'secondary thickenings' example is unclear.

Ambiguous. In the examples it is a collar of the anther ('collar de la antera') and a ring of hairs. PO's leaf collar is the grass leaf blade/sheath junction. Only a word next to it (anther, leaf, hairs) can say which.

Ambiguous. 'Ray' can be an umbel or anthela branch, a ray floret or a ray of wood. Counts of 39-69 do not suit umbel rays in most families. Only 'amount' is attached, and there is no context to choose.

Latin for 'sheath'. In diagnoses it can be a leaf sheath (PO_0020104), a stipular sheath or an ochrea (FLOPO_0986040). A sheath only 1.5-2 mm long is unlikely to be a grass leaf sheath. The genitive that follows it (foliorum, stipularum) has to choose.

A specific structure of one flora (Mimosoideae): a small point on the leaf rachis, at its apex or between pinna pairs. 'Present' and 'amount' rule out mapping it to the rachis apex. It could become a class 'rachis spicule' (part_of leaf rachis PO_0020055) if more floras use it, but that is not shown yet.

'Scale' was rejected in the earlier review as a generic part that needs the organ it belongs to, so its margin is just as unresolved. Once the scale grounds from context, the margin is plant organ margin (PO_0025005) part of that class.

'Ocelo' (eye-spot) is used for different things in different groups: a glandular dot on leaves, a spot on a petal, or a structure on a bract. Only presence is recorded, and the organ cannot be found from the word.
not a part: Fragment of a ratio statement ('1/2 as long to as long as the spikelet'). It is the reference measure of pattern 10, with spikelet (PO_0009051) as the reference part, not a bearer.

Ambiguous within this flora. Some examples are the grass/sedge spikelet axis ('fragile', 'persistent'; spikelet rachilla PO_0009080 already has 'spikelet rhachilla'). Others are the palm ultimate inflorescence branch ('unarmed or with short prickles', 5.5-17 cm long; higher order inflorescence axis PO_0009081). Map it by family, not with one rule.
'Operculum' is ambiguous without the taxon: spore capsule operculum PO_0030044 (mosses), fruit operculum PO_0025298, or calyptra calyx PO_0025329 (Myrtaceae). Fimbriate/membranous does not decide it.

not a part: A fragment that names the whole of a count, not the part counted ('floral scales 4–9 per spikelet'). The bearer is the preceding noun, linked by part_of to spikelet (PO_0009051) under pattern 03 (count of parts).
not a part: A fragment that names the whole of a count ('male flowers 1–4 per fascicle'). The bearer is the preceding noun, linked by part_of to the fascicle (pattern 03).

Ambiguous whole: 'utricle' may be the fruit (PO_0030097) or the Carex perigynium (PO_0009044). 'Appendix' is a generic outgrowth with no class (the earlier review rejected 'appendage'). The source flora is needed.
A generic outgrowth without its organ. Acicular, truncate or deciduous could fit an anther, a fruit or a bract.

not a part: A dimension, not a part: the length of the frond (vascular leaf, PO_0009025, which has 'frond' as a synonym). Here it is the comparand of a ratio (pattern 10: 'stipe 2/3-3/4 the frond length').
not a part: Fragment: the container of a count (pattern 03/14), not a structure. Treated like 'per flower' and 'per node' in the previous review.
not a part: Fragment: the container of a count (sori per pinnule; pinnule is leaflet PO_0020049). Treated like 'per pinna' in the previous review.
Ambiguous: 'flank' means the side of whatever is being described (a lip, glume, keel, fruit or ridge). The values given (violet, inflexed, ascending) fit several of these.
not a part: Fragment: the container of a count (pattern 03/14).
not a part: Fragment: the container of a count (pattern 03/14).
not a part: A unit of area density, not a structure. Rates are held by pattern 14.

Ambiguous: it is either the sheath of a cauline leaf on a culm (leaf sheath, PO_0020104) or a sheathing bract or scale leaf on a scape ('scapi vaginis', which would be scale leaf PO_0006003). The two are different classes, and the word alone does not decide between them.
The organ is not named. The colours (blue-green, pale green) and 'acute' could belong to a leaf, a sepal, a keel or a seed. An abaxial epidermis can only be chosen once the organ is known.
not a part: A fragment: the container of a count ('seeds 1 per fruit'). Pattern 03 should read it with fruit as the container, not as a bearer.

The Spanish 'laminar(es) margen(es) escama(s)' can mean scales on the margin of a leaf lamina or the margin of a scale's own lamina. The values (glabrous, shape) don't settle which. 'Scale' is already a trichome synonym (PO_0000282), but the organ that carries it is unclear.

A hypopodium is the axis below the prophylls. Floras use it for the basal internode of a lateral shoot, or for the part of a pedicel or inflorescence branch below its bracteoles. The examples (2-7 cm × 0.5-1 mm, light pink, velutinous) don't say which axis is meant. If the flora's family is known, it could become shoot axis internode (PO_0005005) or pedicel (PO_0009052) in basal position.
Spanish 'vaina' can mean a leaf sheath (PO_0020104), the sheathing cataphylls on orchid pseudobulbs ('revestido de 3 vainas'), or a legume pod. Without context the bearer can't be chosen.
not a part: A count fragment ('Sori one to each lobe', 'each with 3-4 spines'). It is a container phrase like the rejected 'per node' and 'per ocreate fascicle'; the lobe's organ is not named.

not a part: A fragment: 'per sorus' (por soro), badly stemmed. It is the container phrase of a count: 'sporangia 6-36 per sorus' counts sporangia (PO_0025094) with sorus (PO_0025359) as container (pattern 03 / 14).

A general small point that needs the organ it belongs to. Same decision as for apiculus, apiculum, apicula and mucro in flora_rejected_bearer_words.tsv. Where the organ is named, read it as that organ + apiculate, with the length as a length of the organ's apex. PO has apiculus classes only for the palea (PO_0006033) and the lemma (PO_0025616).

Cells on the dorsal side of some unnamed organ (a bryophyte leaf, an indusium, a trap?). 'fragile', 'inflated' and sizes in µm don't settle which organ, and there are no FLOPO cell classes for a dorsal position. Needs context.

A coloured zone (spot or line) on a tepal, petal or corolla throat; which organ carries it is often not stated ('above claws'). In line with 'eye', rejected as unclear in flora_rejected_bearer_words.tsv. Where the organ is named, read the colour as a colour of that organ. A PO class (part of the perianth) could be proposed if several floras need it.

Two parts measured together (Aristolochia: 'ovary and pedicel 3-5 cm'). No pattern expresses a length summed over two parts, and giving the length to either part alone would be wrong. Keep these as RDF records only.

not a part: A quality and a fragment. The examples mix glandular trichomes ('tricomas glandulares'), sessile glands and glandular punctations (Asteraceae). The full phrase should be grounded per statement: glandular trichome PO_0004509 or a glandular quality of the part that bears them.

Ambiguous between groups. In Bryoerythrophyllum (a moss) these are the ventral surface cells of the costa. In Ceratolejeunea (a liverwort) they are cells of the lobule or the ventral side of the leaf. Different structures under one name, so it needs context per flora.

The space between ribs, with no organ named: it could be on the calyx (e.g. Plumbaginaceae, 'membranous hyaline intervals'), a mericarp (between ridges) or a pappus. The record's context is needed. A bare 'interval' must not become a bearer.
not a part: A count container ('Leaves 3-6 per culm'), like 'per fertile culm' and 'per node'. The leaf is the bearer; the culm (stem PO_0009047) is only the whole.
not a part: A count container ('ovules 2-3 per placenta'), like 'per valve' and 'per lumen'. The bearer is the ovule (PO_0020003); placenta (PO_0025078) is the whole.
Ambiguous: persistent fibres 0.2 mm wide are remains of leaf sheaths or leaf margins (palms, Yucca, Agave), not plant fiber cells (PO_0025407). The organ they come from is not named.

Ambiguous without context. It could be the mouth of a corolla, calyx, pitcher, perianth tube or fruit, and 'vertical', 'oblique' and 'blunt' do not settle which. The organ-named forms ('pitcher mouth', 'corolla orifice') are handled separately.

The examples count rows of small, firm-walled cells, but they do not say which structure the rows belong to (leaf border, capsule mouth, etc.). A row is a way cells are arranged, not a part. Without the whole it cannot be grounded.
not a part: A fragment of a counting phrase ('spores 64 per sporangium'). The counted part is the spore (rule C259) within a sporangium (PO_0025094), as with 'per node' and 'per flower'.
not a part: A fragment of a relative measure ('1/4 de la longitud de la corola'). The bearer is the corolla, and length is the quality.

A diaspore is a dispersal unit. It can be a seed, a fruit, a mericarp or a fruit with its persistent perianth, and the lexicon lists it as a synonym of both seed (PO_0009010) and fruit (PO_0009001). Which one is meant depends on the taxon, so it should be resolved from context, not by one rule.

not a part: A quality word (dentate), not a part. The examples ('teeth of wings', 'dientes ... long') name teeth of unstated organs; those need the organ from context, e.g. leaf lamina tooth (PO_0025518).
not a part: A fragment of a ratio ('petiole length 25-33% of blade'). This belongs to pattern 10 (ratio to another part), with leaf lamina as the reference part.
The apical tooth could belong to a leaf, bract, calyx or spathe ('up to 1.5-2 cm long, incurved'). It cannot be assigned without context.
'1 diente(s) dorsal(es)': the organ that bears the teeth is not given (glume, lemma, anther, perianth?). It cannot be assigned without context.

It could be the calyptra or operculum of Eucalyptus (PO_0025329 or PO_0025330), fruit operculum (PO_0025298) or spore capsule operculum (PO_0030044). 'Conoid, beaked' fits both a Eucalyptus operculum and a moss capsule lid, so the flora's group must decide.
not a part: Aestivation is the arrangement of the perianth in bud (valvate, imbricate), so it is a quality, not a part. Its bearer is the perianth of the female flower (pattern 12).
not a part: Ptyxis is how a single leaf is folded or rolled in bud (inflexed, erect), so it is a quality of the leaf, not a part. 'Reddish-brown' is probably a mis-split statement.

'Wing' was rejected earlier as a generic part. 'Wing 6-7 µm at level of pores' suggests a wing or saccus of pollen rather than of a spore, so the bearer is uncertain. No class exists, and the item comes from only one flora.

Ambiguous. The examples ('réceptacle discoïde', 1 cm wide) fit both a flower receptacle in fruit (PO_0009064, e.g. Annonaceae) and the inflorescence receptacle of Moraceae (Dorstenia). PO_0009064 is the flower receptacle only. Each statement needs its family to be grounded.
not a part: This is a character heading ('posición'), not a structure. The bearer is the inflorescence and the values are its position qualities.

A hyaline apical appendage of the leaf in one flora. It is not clear whether it is a mucro, a hair point or an extension of the sheath. It is not the leaf apex itself, and no existing class fits safely.
not a part: An adjective fragment ('petaline claw', 'lip'). The bearer is in the following noun.
not a part: A ratio fragment ('internodes 1-5 times as long as leaves'). The bearer is the internode and the quality is a relative length.
Only present/absent statements, with no context showing which structure is meant (a bladder, a vesicular hair, or a sac on a seed or fruit).
The margin of a wing, but the wing could be a seed wing (FLOPO_0986091), a fruit wing or a wing petal (PO_0025325). It needs the organ from the context.
